authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Is 1.5x Higher Than In 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Experts feared shortages; cereal production climbed 1.5 times instead.
says: Secondary-school progression rose from 77.8% in 1985 to 91.3% in 2017. More students kept moving forward.
Cereal production climbed from 1083.7 million metric tons in 1972 to 1644.1 million in 2024. Output outran the shortage warnings.
China leads at 5.2 million square kilometers, the United States 4.2, Australia 3.6, Brazil 2.4, and Russia 2.2. Farmland shapes food supply.
authored_explainer.closing: Food scarcity forecasts missed how quickly farming and access could improve.
authored_explainer.question: Which food number surprised you?

authored_explainer.title: Waste Energy Is 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
authored_explainer.hook: Waste—not solar or wind—reached 30.1% of total energy.
says: Combustible renewables and waste rose from 10.2% in 1990 to 30.1% in 2024—3.0 times higher. Discarded material became major fuel.
Electricity access rose from 73.2% in 1998 to 91.9% in 2024—1.3 times higher. Power reached more people.
Waste methane (CH4) rose from 903.8 Mt CO2e in 1972 to 1,652 in 2024—1.8 times higher. The climate cost grew too.
authored_explainer.closing: Turning waste into energy helps, but its emissions still land on everyone.
authored_explainer.question: Should waste count as renewable?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population kept rising, but its growth rate fell 54%.
says: Rural population fell from 63.1% in 1972 to 42.2% in 2025—67 percent of its old share. Humanity moved toward cities.
Largest-city population barely shifted from 18.2% in 1972 to 16.2% in 2025. Urban growth spread beyond one dominant city.
Population growth fell from 2% in 1972 to 0.91% in 2025—46 percent of its old pace. The acceleration nearly stopped.
authored_explainer.closing: Slower growth will reshape schools, jobs, housing, and retirement for everyone.
authored_explainer.question: Where will slower growth hit first?
